newsitem.title: JAPAN: Judge, lawyers trade charges in Japan subway trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge, lawyers trade charges in Japan subway trial.

text.p: Defence lawyers and the chief judge in the trial of the doomsday cult guru accused of the Tokyo subway gas attack on Thursday traded charges about misconduct of the hearing.
In a sign of how heated the row has become, the lawyers announced they would boycott Friday's session of the murder trial of Shoko Asahara, leader of Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect).
Chief defence lawyer Osamu Watanabe told a news conference the boycott was to protest what he said was the unfairly fast pace of the proceedings, which could only lead to Asahara's conviction.
"We won't accept being told to get all the documents together and check the evidence quickly, just to lead to a guilty verdict," he said.

Asahara, on trial on 16 charges ranging from murder to drugs and weapons production, faces death by hanging if found guilty of the March 1995 sarin nerve gas subway attack which killed 12 people and harmed 6,000.
Watanabe said his defence team was ready to stick with Asahara's trial for 10 years despite efforts by Tokyo District Court Chief Judge Fumihiro Abe to speed up proceedings.
"All (Abe) seems to talk about is speeding up the schedule of the trial. We are ready to take over 10 years to gather and scrutinise the necessary evidence and present our case," he said.
Abe responded to the boycott plan with a stern 10-minute lecture to the lawyers at the end of Thursday's hearing in which he accused them of over-detailed and pointless questioning.
"The most important thing is to make the points of the questioning clear. The defence has yet to make the points clear," Abe said.
He also pointed to defence delays in accepting evidence as another factor slowing the trial.
"It's difficult to judge how much time the trial is going to take," Abe said.
